subject: math
title: Telling Time: Clocks, a.m. and p.m., Elapsed Time and Timers
seo_title: Grade 3 Telling Time Worksheets: Analog and Digital Clocks, Elapsed Time and Timers (Free, Ontario)
standard_text: Use analog and digital clocks and timers to tell time in hours, minutes, and seconds
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on telling time for the Ontario curriculum: read analog clocks to the 5 minutes and to the minute, match analog and digital clocks, a.m. and p.m., elapsed time, and timers in seconds. 100 questions with an answer key, good practice for EQAO.
key_big: Short hand: the hour. Long hand: count by 5s, then by 1s.
key_sub: 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds, not 100. If the short hand has not reached a number yet, it is still the hour before. a.m. is midnight to noon; p.m. is noon to midnight.
body_html:
Hours and minutes on an analog clock

The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes. When the long hand goes all the way around once, 60 minutes pass. In that time the short hand moves from one number to the next: 60 minutes = 1 hour.

Each number on the clock is 5 minutes for the long hand, so count by 5s.

Past and to

When the long hand is on the right side, say minutes past the hour. When it is on the left side, say minutes to the next hour.

DigitalWe say
4:004 o’clock
4:15quarter past 4
4:2020 past 4
4:30half past 4
4:3525 to 5
4:45quarter to 5
4:5010 to 5

To the nearest minute

Between two numbers there are 5 small marks, one for each minute. Count by 5s to the last number, then by 1s.

Read to the minute

The long hand is 2 small marks past the 7. The short hand is between 4 and 5.

Count by 5s to the 7: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. Then 36, 37. The hour is still 4.

Answer: 4:37

a.m. and p.m.

A digital clock shows the hour, then a colon, then the minutes. a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).

a.m. or p.m.?

Maya eats breakfast at 25 to 8. Write the time.

25 to 8 is 35 minutes past 7. Breakfast is in the morning, so it is a.m.

Answer: 7:35 a.m.

Elapsed time: how long?

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Jump to the next o’clock first, then on to the end time.

Same hour

Recess is from 10:15 a.m. to 10:30 a.m. How long is it?

30 − 15 = 15

Answer: 15 minutes

Timers and seconds

1 minute = 60 seconds. A stopwatch hand goes once around in 60 seconds, and its numbers count by 5s. A digital timer shows minutes, a colon, then seconds: 1:30 is 1 minute 30 seconds = 90 seconds.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping the hands: reading 8:35 as 7:40The short hand is the hour. The long hand is the minutes
Short hand just before 9 read as 9:35The short hand has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is still 8: 8:35
Long hand on 4 read as 4 minutesEach number is 5 minutes: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes
Breakfast at 7:30 p.m.Morning times are a.m.: 7:30 a.m.
10:50 to 11:20 worked out as 1120 − 1050 = 70 minutesAn hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Count on: 10 + 20 = 30 minutes
1 minute 20 seconds = 120 secondsA minute has 60 seconds: 60 + 20 = 80 seconds

faq.q: What should a Grade 3 student know about time in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario math curriculum (expectation E2.6), Grade 3 students use analog and digital clocks and timers to tell time in hours, minutes and seconds.

faq.q: What is the difference between a.m. and p.m.?
faq.a: a.m. times are from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. times are from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening), so school starts at an a.m. time and dinner is at a p.m. time.

faq.q: Is telling time on the Grade 3 EQAO math assessment?
faq.a: The Grade 3 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum expectations, and using clocks and timers is one of them. Practising clocks, a.m. and p.m., and elapsed time is good preparation.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn to tell time?
faq.a: Keep an analog clock at home and ask the time at everyday moments, such as breakfast or bedtime. Start with o’clock and half past, then count by 5s, then by 1s, and use a kitchen timer to feel how long 60 seconds is.

sets.title: Reading analog clocks to the 5 minutes

items.e: The short hour hand points to 1. The long minute hand points to 12, so it is exactly on the hour. So the time is 1:00. (Not 12:05: that swaps the hands. Not 1:12: when the long hand points to 12, it is 0 minutes.)

The short hour hand points to 2. The long minute hand points to 12, so it is exactly on the hour. So the time is 2:00. (Not 12:10: that swaps the hands. Not 2:12: when the long hand points to 12, it is 0 minutes.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8. It has not reached 8 yet, so the hour is 7. The long minute hand points to 6. Count by 5s: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes. So the time is 7:30. (Not 8:30: the hour hand is before 8, so it is not 8 o’clock yet. Not 6:35: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand points to 6. Count by 5s: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes. Half past means 30 minutes past. The hour hand has not reached 9 yet, so it is half past 8, not half past 9.

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand points to 3. Count by 5s: 3 × 5 = 15 minutes. So the time is 11:15. (Not 11:03: each number is 5 minutes, so 3 means 3 × 5 = 15. Not 3:55: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 10 and 11. It has not reached 11 yet, so the hour is 10. The long minute hand points to 3. Count by 5s: 3 × 5 = 15 minutes. 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour. The long hand is on the right side, so we say past. It is quarter past 10.

The short hour hand is between 4 and 5. It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is 4. The long minute hand points to 9. Count by 5s: 9 × 5 = 45 minutes. So the time is 4:45. (Not 5:45: the hour hand is before 5, so it is not 5 o’clock yet. Not 9:20: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand points to 9. Count by 5s: 9 × 5 = 45 minutes. 45 minutes past 11 is 15 minutes before 12 o’clock. The long hand is on the left side, so we say to the next hour: quarter to 12.

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. The long minute hand points to 1. Count by 5s: 1 × 5 = 5 minutes. So the time is 2:05. (Not 2:01: each number is 5 minutes, so 1 means 1 × 5 = 5. Not 1:10: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4. It has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is 3. The long minute hand points to 2. Count by 5s: 2 × 5 = 10 minutes. So the time is 3:10. (Not 3:02: each number is 5 minutes, so 2 means 2 × 5 = 10. Not 2:15: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. The long minute hand points to 4. Count by 5s: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes. So the time is 1:20. (Not 1:04: each number is 5 minutes, so 4 means 4 × 5 = 20. Not 4:05: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand points to 5. Count by 5s: 5 × 5 = 25 minutes. So the time is 6:25. (Not 6:05: each number is 5 minutes, so 5 means 5 × 5 = 25. Not 5:30: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6. It has not reached 6 yet, so the hour is 5. The long minute hand points to 7. Count by 5s: 7 × 5 = 35 minutes. So the time is 5:35. (Not 6:35: the hour hand is before 6, so it is not 6 o’clock yet. Not 7:25: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1. It has not reached 1 yet, so the hour is 12. The long minute hand points to 8. Count by 5s: 8 × 5 = 40 minutes. So the time is 12:40. (Not 1:40: the hour hand is before 1, so it is not 1 o’clock yet. Not 8:00: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand points to 10. Count by 5s: 10 × 5 = 50 minutes. So the time is 6:50. (Not 7:50: the hour hand is before 7, so it is not 7 o’clock yet. Not 10:30: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand points to 11. Count by 5s: 11 × 5 = 55 minutes. So the time is 6:55. (Not 7:55: the hour hand is before 7, so it is not 7 o’clock yet. Not 11:30: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand points to 4. Count by 5s: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes. The long hand is on the right side, so we say past 11. It is 20 past 11.

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6. It has not reached 6 yet, so the hour is 5. The long minute hand points to 8. Count by 5s: 8 × 5 = 40 minutes. That is 20 minutes before 6 o’clock (60 − 40 = 20). The long hand is on the left side, so we say to 6. It is 20 to 6.

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. The long minute hand points to 7. Count by 5s: 7 × 5 = 35 minutes. So the time is 1:35. (Not 2:35: the hour hand is before 2, so it is not 2 o’clock yet. Not 7:05: that swaps the hands.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8. It has not reached 8 yet, so the hour is 7. The long minute hand points to 10. Count by 5s: 10 × 5 = 50 minutes. That is 10 minutes before 8 o’clock (60 − 50 = 10). The long hand is on the left side, so we say to 8. It is 10 to 8.

sets.title: To the minute: matching analog and digital clocks

items.e: The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 2. Count by 5s to 10, then by 1s: 13 minutes. So the digital time is 6:13. (Not 6:10: count the small marks after the 2 too.)

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 3. Count by 5s to 15, then by 1s: 16 minutes. So the digital time is 11:16. (Not 11:15: count the small marks after the 3 too.)
The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 12: 4 minutes. So the digital time is 11:04.

At 5:38 the long hand is 3 small marks past the 7 (count by 5s to 35, then by 1s to 38), and the short hand is between 5 and 6. That is clock A. (Clock B shows 6:38; clock C shows 5:22; clock D shows 5:07.)

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10. It has not reached 10 yet, so the hour is 9. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 6. Count by 5s to 30, then by 1s: 33 minutes. So the digital time is 9:33. (Not 10:33: the hour hand has not reached 10 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 4 and 5. It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is 4. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 9. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 48 minutes. So the digital time is 4:48. (Not 5:48: the hour hand has not reached 5 yet.)

items.q: How do we say this digital time in words?
items.e: 7:48 is 48 minutes past 7. That is after half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 48 = 12 minutes to 8: 12 minutes to 8.

At 8:13 the long hand is 3 small marks past the 2 (count by 5s to 10, then by 1s to 13), and the short hand is between 8 and 9. That is clock B. (Clock A shows 9:13; clock C shows 8:47; clock D shows 8:02.)

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4. It has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is 3. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 4. Count by 5s to 20, then by 1s: 23 minutes. So the digital time is 3:23. (Not 3:20: count the small marks after the 4 too.)

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 6. Count by 5s to 30, then by 1s: 32 minutes. So the digital time is 8:32. (Not 9:32: the hour hand has not reached 9 yet.)

items.q: Write 23 minutes to 6 as a digital time.
items.e: “23 minutes to 6” means 23 minutes before 6 o’clock. 60 − 23 = 37, so it is 37 minutes past 5: 5:37. (Not 6:37: that would be after 6 o’clock.)

The short hour hand is between 4 and 5. It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is 4. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 11. Count by 5s to 55, then by 1s: 58 minutes. So the digital time is 4:58. (Not 5:58: the hour hand has not reached 5 yet.)

At 6:52 the long hand is 2 small marks past the 10 (count by 5s to 50, then by 1s to 52), and the short hand is between 6 and 7. That is clock D. (Clock A shows 7:52; clock B shows 6:08; clock C shows 6:10.)

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1. It has not reached 1 yet, so the hour is 12. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 6. Count by 5s to 30, then by 1s: 32 minutes. So the digital time is 12:32. (Not 1:32: the hour hand has not reached 1 yet.)

items.q: How do we say this digital time in words?
items.e: 2:14 is 14 minutes after 2 o’clock. It is before half past, so say past: 14 minutes past 2.

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 9. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 48 minutes. So the digital time is 1:48. (Not 2:48: the hour hand has not reached 2 yet.)

At 11:27 the long hand is 2 small marks past the 5 (count by 5s to 25, then by 1s to 27), and the short hand is between 11 and 12. That is clock C. (Clock A shows 12:27; clock B shows 11:33; clock D shows 11:05.)

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10. It has not reached 10 yet, so the hour is 9. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 1. Count by 5s to 5, then by 1s: 6 minutes. So the digital time is 9:06. (Not 9:05: count the small marks after the 1 too.)

items.q: Write 6 minutes past 10 as a digital time.
items.e: “6 minutes past 10” means 6 minutes after 10 o’clock: 10:06.

The short hour hand is between 10 and 11. It has not reached 11 yet, so the hour is 10. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 8. Count by 5s to 40, then by 1s: 41 minutes. So the digital time is 10:41. (Not 11:41: the hour hand has not reached 11 yet.)
a.m. times go from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. times go from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).

c: the end of the school day

items.e: Noon is 12 o’clock in the middle of the day, when the morning ends. 12 o’clock at night is midnight.
The afternoon is after noon, so it is a p.m. time. 2:30 a.m. is in the middle of the night. So the answer is 2:30 p.m.

items.q: Which is a sensible time for school to start?
items.e: School starts in the morning, so it is an a.m. time. 3:45 a.m. is the middle of the night. So the answer is 8:45 a.m.

items.q: Kai eats breakfast at 7:15 in the morning. Is that a.m. or p.m.?
c: a.m., because it is before noon
p.m., because it is before noon
a.m., because it is after noon
p.m., because it is after noon
items.e: Morning times are before noon. Times before noon are a.m. times. So breakfast is at 7:15 a.m.

items.q: Which is earlier in the same day: 11:50 a.m. or 1:10 p.m.?
items.e: a.m. times come before noon and p.m. times come after noon. So 11:50 a.m. is earlier, even though 11 is bigger than 1.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8. It has not reached 8 yet, so the hour is 7. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 12: 2 minutes. It is in the morning, so it is a.m. So the time is 7:02 a.m. (Not 7:02 p.m.: that is in the afternoon or evening.)

items.q: Write quarter to 8 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “quarter to 8” means 15 minutes before 8 o’clock. 60 − 15 = 45, so it is 45 minutes past 7: 7:45. It is in the morning, so it is a.m.: 7:45 a.m.

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1. It has not reached 1 yet, so the hour is 12. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 4. Count by 5s to 20, then by 1s: 24 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 12:24 p.m. (Not 12:24 a.m.: that is in the middle of the night.)

items.q: Write 25 to 4 in the afternoon as a digital time.
items.e: “25 to 4” means 25 minutes before 4 o’clock. 60 − 25 = 35, so it is 35 minutes past 3: 3:35. It is in the afternoon, so it is p.m.: 3:35 p.m.

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 2. Count by 5s to 10, then by 1s: 14 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 6:14 p.m. (Not 6:14 a.m.: that is in the morning.)

items.q: Write 20 past 7 in the evening as a digital time.
items.e: “20 past 7” means 20 minutes after 7 o’clock: 7:20. It is in the evening, so it is p.m.: 7:20 p.m.

The short hour hand is between 4 and 5. It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is 4. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 2. Count by 5s to 10, then by 1s: 13 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 4:13 p.m. (Not 4:13 a.m.: that is in the middle of the night.)

items.q: Write 10 to 11 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “10 to 11” means 10 minutes before 11 o’clock. 60 − 10 = 50, so it is 50 minutes past 10: 10:50. It is in the morning, so it is a.m.: 10:50 a.m.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 4. Count by 5s to 20, then by 1s: 21 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 8:21 p.m. (Not 8:21 a.m.: that is in the morning.)

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 2. Count by 5s to 10, then by 1s: 14 minutes. It is in the morning, so it is a.m. So the time is 8:14 a.m. (Not 8:14 p.m.: that is in the afternoon or evening.)

items.q: How many hours is it from 9:00 a.m. to noon?
items.e: Count the jumps, not the numbers: 9:00 → 10:00 → 11:00 → 12:00 noon. That is 3 hours. (4 counts the numbers 9, 10, 11 and 12.)

items.q: How many hours is it from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.?
items.e: 11:00 a.m. → 12:00 noon is 1 hour. 12:00 noon → 2:00 p.m. is 2 hours. 1 + 2 = 3 hours. (Not 9 hours: 11 − 2 = 9 does not work across noon.)

items.q: Put these times in order from earliest to latest in one day: 3:00 p.m., 7:00 a.m., 9:30 p.m., 11:00 a.m.
items.e: All a.m. times come first, then the p.m. times. a.m.: 7:00, then 11:00. p.m.: 3:00, then 9:30. So the order is 7:00 a.m., 11:00 a.m., 3:00 p.m., 9:30 p.m.

items.q: A digital clock shows 4:37 p.m. How many minutes is it until 5:00 p.m.?
items.e: An hour has 60 minutes. It is 37 minutes past 4. 60 − 37 = 23 minutes until 5:00 p.m. (Not 63: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

sets.title: Elapsed time in minutes and hours

items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 30 − 15 = 15 minutes.

items.q: Gym class starts at 1:05 p.m. and ends at 1:45 p.m. How long is gym class?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 5 = 40 minutes.
Both times are in the same hour. 35 − 10 = 25 minutes.

items.q: Olivia gets on the school bus at 8:12 a.m. She gets to school at 8:31 a.m. How long is the bus ride?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 31 − 12 = 19 minutes.
The minutes are the same, so count the hours. Count the jumps, not the numbers: 9:00 a.m. → 10:00 a.m. That is 1 hour. (1 hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: The bus for the field trip leaves at 9:00 a.m. It gets to the museum at 11:00 a.m. How long is the bus ride?
items.e: The minutes are the same, so count the hours. Count the jumps, not the numbers: 9:00 a.m. → 10:00 a.m. → 11:00 a.m. That is 2 hours. (1 hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Recess starts at 10:15 a.m. It lasts 15 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Count on 15 minutes from 10:15: 15 + 15 = 30. It is still the morning, so recess ends at 10:30 a.m. (11:15 a.m. would be 1 hour later.)

items.q: Lunch starts at 11:40 a.m. and ends at 12:20 p.m. How long is lunch?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 11:40 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 20 minutes. Then 12:00 noon to 12:20 p.m. is 20 minutes. 20 + 20 = 40 minutes. (Not 80 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Maya skates at the rink from 3:50 p.m. to 4:15 p.m. How long does she skate?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 3:50 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 10 minutes. Then 4:00 p.m. to 4:15 p.m. is 15 minutes. 10 + 15 = 25 minutes. (Not 65 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Lucas’s swimming lesson is from 4:45 p.m. to 5:20 p.m. How long is it?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 4:45 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 15 minutes. Then 5:00 p.m. to 5:20 p.m. is 20 minutes. 15 + 20 = 35 minutes. (Not 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Nathan goes to bed at 8:30 p.m. He reads for 20 minutes before bed. What time does he start reading?
items.e: Count back 20 minutes from 8:30: 30 − 20 = 10. Reading starts at 8:10 p.m. (8:50 p.m. is 20 minutes after bedtime.)

items.q: Art starts at 1:40 p.m. It lasts 50 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: From 1:40 p.m., 20 minutes takes you to 2:00 p.m. 50 − 20 = 30 more minutes makes 2:30 p.m. (2:40 p.m. would be 1 hour later, not 50 minutes.)

items.q: A hockey game starts at 6:30 p.m. and ends at 8:00 p.m. How long is the game?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 6:30 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 30 minutes. Then 7:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. is 1 hour. 30 + 60 = 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes.

items.q: A movie starts at 7:00 p.m. and ends at 8:45 p.m. How long is the movie?
items.e: From 7:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. is 1 hour. Then 8:00 p.m. to 8:45 p.m. is 45 minutes. So it is 1 hour 45 minutes.

items.q: The maple syrup festival is open from 10:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. How long is it open?
items.e: The minutes are the same, so count the hours. Count the jumps, not the numbers: 10:30 a.m. → 11:30 a.m. → 12:30 p.m. → 1:30 p.m. That is 3 hours. (1 hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Noah’s soccer game starts at 6:10 p.m. He leaves home 25 minutes before the game. What time does he leave home?
items.e: Count back 10 minutes to 6:00 p.m. 25 − 10 = 15, so count back 15 more minutes: 5:45 p.m. (6:35 p.m. is 25 minutes after 6:10.)

items.q: The bus for the field trip leaves at 9:20 a.m. The ride takes 1 hour 25 minutes. What time does the bus arrive?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 9:20 a.m. → 10:20 a.m. Then add 25 minutes: 20 + 25 = 45. The bus arrives at 10:45 a.m.

items.q: School starts at 8:45 a.m. and ends at 3:15 p.m. How long is the school day?
items.e: 8:45 a.m. to 2:45 p.m. is 6 hours. 2:45 p.m. to 3:15 p.m. is 30 minutes. So the school day is 6 hours 30 minutes. (Not 7 hours: 8:45 to 3:45 would be 7 hours, but school ends 30 minutes before 3:45.)

items.q: Leah’s movie is 1 hour 30 minutes long. Owen’s movie is 95 minutes long. Whose movie is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 1 hour 30 minutes = 60 + 30 = 90 minutes. 95 − 90 = 5. So Owen’s movie is longer, by 5 minutes. (Not Leah’s by 35: that counts an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: On Thanksgiving, the turkey goes in the oven at 11:30 a.m. It cooks for 3 hours 15 minutes. What time is it ready?
items.e: Add 3 hours: 11:30 a.m. → 12:30 p.m. → 1:30 p.m. → 2:30 p.m. Then add 15 minutes: 2:45 p.m. It is after noon, so it is p.m.
There are 60 seconds in 1 minute. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)
The numbers on a stopwatch count by 5s. The hand points to 35, so it shows 35 seconds. (Not 7: 35 is the 7th number, but each number is 5 seconds.)

items.q: The class does a 60-second challenge. Priya does jumping jacks until the timer beeps. How long is that?
items.e: 60 seconds = 1 minute. (60 minutes would be 1 hour.)
1 minute = 60 seconds. 2 minutes = 60 + 60 = 120 seconds. (Not 200: a minute is not 100 seconds.)
The hand is 2 small marks past the 45. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 46, 47. It shows 47 seconds. (A stopwatch hand that goes once around in 60 seconds shows seconds, not minutes.)

items.q: The timer shows minutes and seconds. How many seconds is that?
items.e: 1:20 means 1 minute 20 seconds. 1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 + 20 = 80 seconds. (Not 120: a minute is 60 seconds, not 100.)

items.q: Which unit would you use to time a 50 m race in gym class?
items.e: A 50 m race is over very fast, in less than a minute. We time it in seconds.

items.q: Which is the same as 90 seconds?
items.e: 60 seconds make 1 minute. 90 − 60 = 30 seconds left. So 90 seconds = 1 minute 30 seconds. (1 minute 10 seconds would be 70 seconds.)

items.q: About how long does it take to tie your shoes?
items.e: Tying shoes is quick. 30 minutes is much too long. It takes about 30 seconds.
2 minutes = 60 + 60 = 120 seconds. 120 seconds is more than 100 seconds, so 2 minutes is longer.

items.q: In the 60-second challenge, Arjun has used 45 seconds. How many seconds are left?
items.e: 60 − 45 = 15 seconds. (55 would be 100 − 45, but a minute has 60 seconds.)

items.q: A timer starts at 1:00 and counts down. What does it show after 25 seconds?
items.e: 1:00 is 1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 − 25 = 35 seconds left, so it shows 0:35. (0:75 comes from 100 − 25, but there are only 60 seconds in a minute.)

items.q: Popcorn cooks in the microwave for 2 minutes 30 seconds. How many seconds is that?
items.e: 2 minutes = 120 seconds. 120 + 30 = 150 seconds. (230 counts a minute as 100 seconds.)

items.q: Jayden skates 1 lap of the rink in 40 seconds. How long do 3 laps take?
items.e: 40 + 40 + 40 = 120 seconds. 120 seconds = 60 + 60 = 2 minutes. (1 minute 20 seconds counts a minute as 100 seconds.)

items.q: Mom sets a timer for 12 minutes at 2:40 p.m. to bake maple cookies. When does the timer beep?
items.e: Count on 12 minutes from 2:40: 40 + 12 = 52. It is the afternoon, so the timer beeps at 2:52 p.m.

items.q: At the Terry Fox Run, Benjamin runs the first part in 58 seconds. Chloe takes 1 minute 5 seconds. How much faster is Benjamin?
items.e: 1 minute 5 seconds = 60 + 5 = 65 seconds. 65 − 58 = 7 seconds. (Not 47: a minute is 60 seconds, not 100.)

items.q: Hana holds a plank for 1 minute 20 seconds. Aiden holds it for 55 seconds. How much longer is Hana’s plank?
items.e: 1 minute 20 seconds = 60 + 20 = 80 seconds. 80 − 55 = 25 seconds. (65 comes from 120 − 55, which counts a minute as 100 seconds.)

items.q: Ava’s time in a ringette drill is 1 minute 15 seconds. Amira’s time is 70 seconds. Who is faster?
items.e: 1 minute 15 seconds = 60 + 15 = 75 seconds. 70 is less than 75, so Amira is faster, by 75 − 70 = 5 seconds. (A faster time is a smaller number.)

items.q: On a snow day, hot chocolate heats in the microwave for 1 minute 30 seconds. 50 seconds have passed. How much time is left?
items.e: 1 minute 30 seconds = 60 + 30 = 90 seconds. 90 − 50 = 40 seconds. (80 comes from 130 − 50, which counts a minute as 100 seconds.)

items.q: The oven timer shows how long until the cookies are done. How many seconds is that?
items.e: 2:45 means 2 minutes 45 seconds. 2 minutes = 120 seconds. 120 + 45 = 165 seconds. (245 counts a minute as 100 seconds.)
